meaning:
ἀπ-αλλάσσω
[in LXX for סוּר hi., etc. ;]
to remove, release: Heb.2:15; pass., to depart: Act.19:12; in legal sense (MM, VGT, see word), before ἀπό, with genitive of person(s), to be quit of: Luk.12:58 (Cremer, 90, 632).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and…
so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.
and might deliver all of them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
